function_v0.doc:
One-shot, admin-gated init. The market **discovers** PT, YT, the asset and expiry from the
series, and checks that the claim tokens point back at it, so it cannot be wired to a
foreign settlement asset (`tofix.md` #19's class).

* `scalar_root` \xe2\x80\x94 curve steepness (price impact only; the anchor is dynamic). YT price
impact is large because a small PT price move is a big share of YT's small price, so a
flatter curve matters more here than on Blend.
* `ln_fee_root` \xe2\x80\x94 **annualized** fee root, SCALAR_12. A YT trader pays roughly
`ln_fee_root \xc3\xb7 yield` of the YT's value per side, which bites harder at USTRY's ~3.5% NAV
growth than on a higher-yield source. Both dials are swept in
`calibrate_the_fee_root_and_scalar_for_ustry`.
* `initial_apy` \xe2\x80\x94 the rate the pool opens at, SCALAR_12 fraction (any seed ratio works).
* `treasury_fee_share_bps` \xe2\x80\x94 protocol share of each swap fee, \xe2\x89\xa4 [`MAX_TREASURY_FEE_SHARE_BPS`].

function_v0.doc:
Add `pt_in` PT and `asset_in` USTRY. The first LP sets the reserve ratio; because the
anchor is dynamic, **any** ratio opens the pool at the configured rate. Later LPs mint
`min(by_pt, by_asset)` and pass `min_shares` as their slippage bound (0 = the pool's own
0.1% ratio band).

**Opening the pool needs the admin's signature as well as the LP's, and a ratio inside the
safe band.** `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` locks a sliver of the first deposit's ratio in the pool for
ever, so a hostile first deposit at an extreme ratio would leave the market permanently
untradeable (proper-test-of-ustry.md M-1; ustry-fixes-2026-11-17.md #2). The two checks are
independent: the band also protects an admin seed from a fat-fingered ratio. The same goes
for reopening a pool every LP has left (only the locked `MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY` shares remain,
so the dust ratio would otherwise let anyone re-seed it). A reopen is priced at the share
price the locked shares imply, so the dust stays locked. Every deposit into a live pool is
permissionless.

function_v0.doc:
**Buy at least `yt_out` YT** (face, USD units). The user funds only the YT's price; the
pool funds the rest of the notional and keeps the freshly split PT.

1. size the split from the factor this market **last observed**. The factor only ever
falls (high-water NAV only rises), so any observed factor is an upper bound and the
split yields \xe2\x89\xa5 `yt_out` face
2. pull the user's `max_asset_in` (not the computed cost \xe2\x80\x94 see below)
3. `deposit_split` the notional to the market. This is the series' strict NAV fold: it
refuses stale or drawdown NAV and leaves the series' state freshly folded
4. price on that **post-split** factor, as "the pool buys every PT just minted": the pool
pays the curve price for `face` PT, the user pays the rest of the notional for `face` YT
5. transfer all `face` YT to the user (the claim token settles both sides), refund the rest

The NAV is folded once per trade (inside the split) instead of twice, and the split is sized
without a separate read \xe2\x80\x94 the two largest avoidable memory costs o
function_v0.name: buy_yt_exact_out

function_v0.doc:
Burn `shares` and return the proportional PT + USTRY. **Open while paused, after expiry,
during an oracle outage and after a clawback** \xe2\x80\x94 it never calls the oracle.

If the pool holds less than its recorded reserves (issuer clawback), each leg is paid
pro-rata from `min(reserve, held)` while the *full* pro-rata claim is retired from the
reserve. That keeps the held/reserve ratio identical for every remaining LP: everyone takes
the same haircut whatever order they leave in, and a later restoration benefits whoever is
still in the pool.
function_v0.name: remove_liquidity

function_v0.doc:
**Sell exactly `yt_in` YT.** The pool contributes matching PT, the pair is recombined
through the series (`redeem` before finalization burns PT + YT), and the released USTRY is
split: the pool keeps the PT's market value, the seller takes the rest.

The seller's accrued yield is settled by the YT transfer in step 1 \xe2\x80\x94 **credited, not paid**.
Collect it with `series.claim_yield`. Needs no fresh NAV (the series' redeem never reads
the oracle); refused only if the series' custody is frozen by a clawback.

Returns the USTRY paid to the seller.

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A single deposit's accounting record \xe2\x80\x94 the unit that makes Spield's yield math correct.

**Per-position, never overwritten** (fixes SCF #4): every `mint` creates a *new* `Position`
with its own `entry_rate`, so topping up never clobbers an earlier tranche's entry point.

**`settled_rate` travels with the YT** (fixes SCF #5/#6): yield is always measured from
`settled_rate`, which starts at `entry_rate` and is bumped to the current rate on every
`claim_yield` *without burning YT*. A position transferred to a new owner carries its
`settled_rate`, so the buyer can only ever claim yield accrued *after* they held it.
udt_struct_v0.name: Position

fields.doc: Blend `b_rate` (SCALAR_12) at the moment this position was minted. Immutable.

fields.name: owner

fields.name: principal

fields.doc: PT still held in this position. Burned on `redeem_pt` (after maturity) and on `combine`.
fields.name: pt_amount

fields.doc: Blend `b_rate` (SCALAR_12) up to which yield has already been settled/paid. Starts equal\nto `entry_rate`; advanced to `current_rate` on each claim. Yield owed is measured from\nhere, so the same YT can be claimed across many epochs.
fields.name: settled_rate

fields.doc: Blend bToken shares this position is backed by (its slice of the wrapper's total Blend\nposition). `principal = shares * entry_rate / SCALAR_12` at mint.
fields.name: shares

fields.doc: YT still held in this position. **Never burned by `claim_yield`** \xe2\x80\x94 only by `combine`.
fields.name: yt_amount

udt_struct_v0.doc:
Defence-in-depth bound on `b_rate` reads, stored in the strategy adapter's config.

The bound is **time-aware**: `b_rate` may rise by at most `max_apr_bps` per year, pro-rated by
the seconds elapsed since `last_ts`. This makes the check independent of how often the strategy
is read (a long-untouched position no longer false-trips), so only `max_apr_bps` \xe2\x80\x94 calibrated
against Blend's real max borrow APR \xe2\x80\x94 needs tuning. See [`crate::math::check_rate_bound_timed`].

fields.name: last_ts

fields.doc: Max allowed **annual** `b_rate` growth, in basis points (e.g. `30_000` = 300% APR). Set\ngenerously above Blend's real max borrow APR so honest reads always pass.

A single Fixed-Rate Vault deposit (plan \xc2\xa711.2 / \xc2\xa77.5 \xe2\x80\x94 the flagship "lock X% fixed" product).
